records.Title: Enterprise architecture function activation
records.Analysis: The EA function is being progressively activated through defined governance models, architecture review processes, and initial onboarding of the EA Tool. The operating model and engagement framework are in use for project/product reviews and portfolio alignment.
records.Challenges: DDA and ARB have been activated. However, Limited operational clarity on ARB & DDA workflows and decision rights. Efforts are ongoing to include the EA Review in the procurement process and to issue a Gov-Digital circular for its official activation.
records.Recommendations: Finalize and implement operational governance workflows. Conduct targeted stakeholder awareness sessions to strengthen adoption. Issue circular for the activation of EA function.

records.Analysis: EA standards and approval workflows have been defined conceptually but not yet fully operationalized. However, few platform/products have been prioritized for EA review.

records.Title: Standard policies issuance
records.Analysis: The standards lifecycle and governance model have been defined, detailing how standards evolve from current to target state. However, the Standard policies issuance is still work in progress.
records.Challenges: Missing operational clarity on maintenance and review cycles. Inconsistent submission from teams affecting baseline completeness. Lack of practical guidance and onboarding materials for policy implementation.
records.Recommendations: Finalize document collection and ownership mapping for current-to-target states.
records.DirectorComments: The EA BOT schedule has been impacted by external procurement delays and dependencies that were outside the delivery team’s direct control. Initial onboarding of key resources faced unexpected contractual and mobilization constraints, which slowed momentum. Additionally, the first deployed team’s deliverable quality required corrective measures to ensure long-term success and alignment with strategic expectations. These combined factors contributed to the 5-month delay while maintaining a strong focus on delivering sustainable, high-quality outcomes

records.Title: Mean time to respond to unauthorized access
records.Analysis: The average response time is approximately 33 minutes, slightly above the 30-minute target. The result demonstrates that the majority of unauthorized access incidents are handled efficiently, with only minimal variance from the target threshold. Continued process streamlining and improved coordination can further enhance response performance.
records.Challenges: Minor delays caused by manual record updates and inconsistent timestamp entries have contributed to small fluctuations in measured response times. Implementing automated timestamp logging and reinforcing prompt data entry will help ensure consistency and reduce overall response time.
records.Recommendations: Automate timestamp and workflow tracking through SIEM and Ticketing tool integration.
